previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, and chronic pulmonary emboli was admitted for progressively severe shortness of breath, chest pressure, and a productive cough. Initial evaluation ruled out pulmonary embolism but revealed worsening interstitial lung disease. Her symptoms were attributed to a flare of polymyositis with lung involvement and possible respiratory infection, though extensive microbiologic testing did not confirm an active infection. She was treated with high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, transitioned to oral steroids, and received a rituximab infusion. Her anticoagulation was managed with heparin bridging and warfarin restart after a bronchoscopy. Iron supplementation was initiated for iron deficiency anemia. By discharge, her respiratory status improved, oxygen requirements decreased to nighttime use, and she was able to ambulate with assistance. She was discharged on increased prednisone, daily Bactrim, iron, and warfarin, with plans for outpatient pulmonary function tests and rheumatology follow-up including a second rituximab infusion.

Brief Hospital Course:
PATIENT: ___ yo F with DM, CHF, h/o PEs on coumadin, and 
polymyositis on steroids/rituxan admitted with right axillary 
abscess.

ACUTE ISSUES:
# Right axillary abscess - The abscess began has a small painful 
carbuncle palpable by the patient, and then grew over the course 
of a few weeks. She reports subjective fevers though afebrile 
throughout her hospitalization. She was started on vancomycin 
for assumed staph infection. Gen surg was consulted, but given 
her size and skin grafts drainage was initially deferred to 
ultrasound-guided inteventional radiology. ___ elected for 
aspiration given her warfarin use and risk for bleeding. She 
underwent aspiratin of ~20cc of pus which grew morganella 
___ (gram neg rod) resistant only to bactrim. Gram stain 
suggested poly-microbrial flora. After the aspiration her WBC 
initially increased so zosyn was added to cover gram negatives. 
She was then transitioned to an oral antibiotic regimen of 
doxycycline, cipro and flagyl to cover gram+, gram-, anaerobes 
and pseudomonas. A repeat ultrasound noted a persistent 
collection, so general surgery was again consulted and elected 
to undergo an incision and drainage. About 2cc were drained from 
the site and the area was packed and dressed. She was discharged 
home to comlete a week of oral antibiotics with daily dressing 
changes.

# Anti-coagulation - Warfarin was initially held on admission 
due to the necessity of the abscess drainage. Warfarin was 
restarted after ___ aspiration, but due to her low INR a bridge 
with heparin drip was also begun. She received two days of 
warfarin 10mg followed by 5mg daily and was therapeutic on 
discharge with an INR of 2.1. ___ will measure INR on follow-up.

CHRONIC ISSUES:
# Polymyositis - continued on home regimen of prednisolone and 
oxygen

# CHF - no evidence for a CHF worsening on this admission. 
continued on home regimen of lasix and metoprolol

# DM - sliding scale insulin while ___ the hospital. continue
